CORAM : JITENDRA JAIN, J.
DATED : 06th APRIL 2026 P. C. :
1. Though respondents have been duly served, there is no appearance on behalf of the respondents.
Since issue involved lies in narrow compass and appeal is of 2020, same is taken up for final hearing.

2. The appellant challenges judgment dated 10th August, 2017 passed by the MACT,
Mumbai, whereby, the application made for compensation of Rs.3 lakhs on account of injury sustained by the appellant, came to be rejected on the ground that the documentary evidence shows that the appellant was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
3. On 25th November, 2004, the appellant alongwith his wife was travelling on motor Shri.

The Toyota Qualis, four wheeler vehicle overtook the appellant's vehicle and applied immediate brakes, which resulted into the appellant's vehicle getting dashed with the Toyota Qualis.
The appellant and his wife suffered injuries.
1 of 3 HMK 33. FA-81-2020.doc
An First Information Report (FIR) came to be filed against the appellant, which was the subject matter of Criminal Case No. 507 of 2005.
Since major injury was suffered by the appellant, he alone filed an application to the Tribunal for the compensation, which came to be rejected.
Therefore, the present Appeal.

4. The Sessions Court by order dated 03 rd January, 2012 acquitted the appellant of all the charges, namely, Section 279, 337 and 338 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC)
and Section 255(1) of the Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988.
The Sessions Court after considering the evidence, has discharged the appellant.

5. It was not the case of benefit of doubt being given to the appellant by the Sessions Court, but it was the case where after considering the evidence, the appellant was acquitted of all the charges, which had culminated into the acquittal of the appellant.
Therefore, the distinction made by the MACT that the documentary evidence has to be given importance as compared to the Sessions Court decision, in my view, is not a correct approach.

The Ho'n'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satish Chander Ahuja vs. Sneha Ahuja1 has analysed this issue on the extent of reliance to be placed on a finding given by the Courts dealing with the criminal matters while deciding the civil matters and vice versa.

entities.text: Satish Chander Ahuja vs. Sneha Ahuja1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In my view, the ratio of the said decision squarely applies to the facts of the present case.
The issue whether the appellant was driving rashly was also the issue before the Sessions Court and, therefore, findings of the Sessions Court are relevant for deciding same issue in civil matter.
6. In view of above, the impugned order to the extent it holds appellant liable for rash and negligent driving is quashed and set aside.

The Original Application No. 308 of 2010 is restored back to the file of the MACT,
Mumbai for adjudicating the amount of compensation.
8. The appellant to appear before the MACT, Mumbai on 27 th April, 2026, so that the Tribunal can fix up a date for hearing of the compensation.
9. Appeal is allowed in above terms.
